item.content:encoded: <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </p> <p>A <strong>Malleable C2 profile</strong> describes configurable aspects of Cobalt Strike communication and related behavior. It changes indicators, but a changed indicator is insufficient evidence of a bypass. This module teaches you to separate configuration validity, successful communication, collected telemetry, and detection outcomes.</p> <p><em>Allow about 20 minutes, plus time for the local HTTP exercise. The exercise sends harmless requests to your own loopback interface and does not deploy an agent.</em></p> <h2 id="what-you-will-learn"> <a href="#what-you-will-learn" title="What You Will Learn">What You Will Learn</a> <a href="#what-you-will-learn" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What You Will Learn">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Define</strong> profiles, transforms, polling, jitter, and observation points.</li> <li><strong>Explain</strong> which parts of an HTTP exchange different sensors observe.</li> <li><strong>Inspect</strong> two local requests and compare their records.</li> <li><strong>Evaluate</strong> the evidence behind a claim of reduced detection.</li> <li><strong>Create</strong> a controlled comparison with explicit assumptions and limits.</li> </ul> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Term</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Profile</strong></td> <td>Configuration describing selected communication and runtime behavior</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Transform</strong></td> <td>Reversible operation used to encode and recover exchanged data</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Polling</strong></td> <td>Checking periodically for work or results</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Jitter</strong></td> <td>Variation applied to a timing interval</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Telemetry</strong></td> <td>Recorded observations of system or network activity</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Detection</strong></td> <td>Logic interpreting observations as a condition of interest</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="understand-profile-scope"> <a href="#understand-profile-scope" title="Understand Profile Scope">Understand Profile Scope</a> <a href="#understand-profile-scope" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Understand Profile Scope">#</a> </h2> <p>The <strong>communication profile</strong> describes where data appears in transactions and how the receiving side recovers it. This is more specific than changing a display name or cosmetic label. Both ends need compatible expectations for the exchange to work. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the Malleable C2 overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://hstechdocs.helpsystems.com/manuals/cobaltstrike/current/userguide/content/topics/malleable-c2_main.htm"> <a href="https://hstechdocs.helpsystems.com/manuals/cobaltstrike/current/userguide/content/topics/malleable-c2_main.htm" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the Malleable C2 overview</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Other profile sections</strong> govern aspects of memory, process injection, and post-exploitation jobs. Keep those settings separate from a claim about network behavior. A change in one category is not evidence of a result in another. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the profile-extension overview"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://hstechdocs.helpsystems.com/manuals/cobaltstrike/current/userguide/content/topics/malleable-c2-extend_main.htm"> <a href="https://hstechdocs.helpsystems.com/manuals/cobaltstrike/current/userguide/content/topics/malleable-c2-extend_main.htm" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the profile-extension overview</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Configuration behavior</strong> is version-specific. The 4.13 documentation introduces overrides for a defined subset of settings when generating new payloads. Check the documented override scope instead of assuming a restart is always required or every running agent inherits an edit. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the override documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://hstechdocs.helpsystems.com/manuals/cobaltstrike/current/userguide/content/topics/malleable-c2_profile-overrides.htm"> <a href="https://hstechdocs.helpsystems.com/manuals/cobaltstrike/current/userguide/content/topics/malleable-c2_profile-overrides.htm" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the override documentation</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Evidence needed</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Was the profile accepted?</strong></td> <td>Validation output and selected configuration</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Did the exchange work?</strong></td> <td>Correct decoded result through the tested path</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>What did a sensor see?</strong></td> <td>Sensor record, configuration, and timestamp</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Did a rule alert?</strong></td> <td>Rule identity, outcome, and evaluation window</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="separate-four-outcomes"> <a href="#separate-four-outcomes" title="Separate Four Outcomes">Separate Four Outcomes</a> <a href="#separate-four-outcomes" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Separate Four Outcomes">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Syntactic validity</strong> means a configuration passed specified checks. <strong>Functional success</strong> means the intended exchange produced the expected result. Neither outcome establishes how a security product classified the activity.</p> <p><strong>Telemetry collection</strong> precedes many detection decisions. A request might be recorded without generating an alert, or an alert might depend on later correlation with endpoint behavior. Report those stages independently so an absence of alerts does not become a claim of invisibility.</p> <p><strong>Response</strong> adds another stage after detection. An analyst’s investigation or a containment action depends on workflow, policy, and available context. A test of network visibility should not silently become a claim about the entire response program.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/profile-observation-and-detection.webp", "caption": "Four connected boxes distinguish accepted configuration, working communication, collected observations, and evaluated detection results", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-22 04:18:56.271443199 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b324.926535636", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-22 04:18:56.271443199 +0000 UTC m=+324.926535636"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/profile-observation-and-detection.webp" alt="Four connected boxes distinguish accepted configuration, working communication, collected observations, and evaluated detection results"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>A pass at one stage leaves the following stage unproven</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="read-http-in-context"> <a href="#read-http-in-context" title="Read HTTP in Context">Read HTTP in Context</a> <a href="#read-http-in-context" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Read HTTP in Context">#</a> </h2> <p>An <strong>HTTP request</strong> includes a method, target, headers, and sometimes content. A user-agent value is supplied by the client and does not authenticate the application sending it. Read the whole exchange and its context before assigning meaning to one field. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the HTTP semantics specification"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"> <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the HTTP semantics specification</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>HTTPS</strong> protects application data in transit between TLS peers. A passive observer outside the TLS session does not ordinarily read its HTTP path and headers, while an endpoint or configured inspection proxy has a different view. State the observation point whenever you discuss visibility. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the TLS 1.3 specification"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446.html"> <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the TLS 1.3 specification</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Network metadata</strong> still carries useful context, including observed endpoints, timing, and traffic sizes. Which names and application details remain exposed depends on the actual protocols and deployment. Do not equate encrypted content with a complete absence of observable behavior.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Observation point</th> <th>Typical evidence</th> <th>Main limitation</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Application server</strong></td> <td>Received request and response outcome</td> <td>Its configured logs omit some fields</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Endpoint sensor</strong></td> <td>Process and connection context</td> <td>Coverage depends on configuration</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Passive network sensor</strong></td> <td>Traffic timing and transport metadata</td> <td>Encrypted application content is restricted</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="check-functional-validity"> <a href="#check-functional-validity" title="Check Functional Validity">Check Functional Validity</a> <a href="#check-functional-validity" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Check Functional Validity">#</a> </h2> <p><strong><code>c2lint</code></strong> is the vendor’s profile-checking tool. It checks syntax and performs additional tests using generated data. Use it as evidence about configuration validity, then validate the actual permitted communication path separately. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the validator documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://hstechdocs.helpsystems.com/manuals/cobaltstrike/current/userguide/content/topics/malleable-c2_checking-errors.htm"> <a href="https://hstechdocs.helpsystems.com/manuals/cobaltstrike/current/userguide/content/topics/malleable-c2_checking-errors.htm" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the validator documentation</a> </span> .</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>./c2lint /path/to/approved-lab.profile </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>The path argument</strong> selects an existing profile for validation. Run the validator supplied with the release under review and retain its output with the profile’s hash. This command checks a file, so it does not prove an agent exchanged tasks through a proxy or a detection rule evaluated the resulting traffic.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Exit code</th> <th>Documented meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>0</strong></td> <td>No reported errors or warnings</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>1</strong></td> <td>Warnings only</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>2</strong></td> <td>Errors only</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>3</strong></td> <td>Both errors and warnings</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Intermediaries</strong> introduce additional variables. A proxy might rewrite a field, enforce a body-size limit, or reject a request under policy. Successful direct communication in a lab is insufficient proof of the same behavior through a different path.</p> <h2 id="inspect-harmless-local-requests"> <a href="#inspect-harmless-local-requests" title="Inspect Harmless Local Requests">Inspect Harmless Local Requests</a> <a href="#inspect-harmless-local-requests" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Inspect Harmless Local Requests">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Create a disposable directory</strong> containing one synthetic text file. The following commands create it under your temporary directory and start Python’s demonstration HTTP server bound to <strong><code>127.0.0.1</code></strong>. The <strong><code>--directory</code></strong> argument limits the served tree to the generated folder. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read Python’s HTTP-server command-line documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.server.html"> <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.server.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read Python’s HTTP-server command-line documentation</a> </span> .</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>lab_dir<span style="color:#f92672">=</span><span style="color:#66d9ef">$(</span>mktemp -d<span style="color:#66d9ef">)</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>printf <span style="color:#e6db74">'synthetic training response\n'</span> > <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$lab_dir<span style="color:#e6db74">/sample.txt"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>python3 -m http.server <span style="color:#ae81ff">8765</span> --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$lab_dir<span style="color:#e6db74">"</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Keep this terminal open</strong> while making the requests below in a second terminal. The server is a local teaching aid, not a production service. If port 8765 is occupied, choose an unused port and update both commands consistently.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>curl --noproxy <span style="color:#e6db74">'*'</span> --verbose <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> --user-agent <span style="color:#e6db74">'CourseLab/1.0'</span> <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> http://127.0.0.1:8765/sample.txt </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>curl --noproxy <span style="color:#e6db74">'*'</span> --verbose <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> --user-agent <span style="color:#e6db74">'CourseLab/2.0'</span> <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> http://127.0.0.1:8765/sample.txt </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong><code>--noproxy '*'</code></strong> bypasses configured proxies for these requests. <strong><code>--verbose</code></strong> prints request and response details, while <strong><code>--user-agent</code></strong> sets the client-supplied header. The response body remains the same synthetic file in both cases. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the curl options reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://curl.se/docs/manpage.html"> <a href="https://curl.se/docs/manpage.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the curl options reference</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Record</th> <th>Expected comparison</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>curl request details</strong></td> <td>User-agent changes between requests</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Response body</strong></td> <td>Same synthetic content</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Default server log</strong></td> <td>Request line and status, without every request header</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Interpret the difference:</strong> a header changed even if the default server log does not display it. Missing fields in a log reflect the record’s coverage, not necessarily the absence of those fields on the wire. These are expected observations for the example, so compare them with your own run and explain any discrepancy.</p> <p><strong>Finish the exercise</strong> by pressing <strong>Ctrl+C</strong> in the server terminal. In the same shell, run <strong><code>printf '%s\n' "$lab_dir"</code></strong> to identify the generated folder and remove only the disposable folder when your notes are saved. This exercise measures HTTP representation and logging coverage, not Cobalt Strike behavior or an EDR result.</p> <h2 id="evaluate-detection-claims"> <a href="#evaluate-detection-claims" title="Evaluate Detection Claims">Evaluate Detection Claims</a> <a href="#evaluate-detection-claims" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Evaluate Detection Claims">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A fair comparison</strong> defines one changed variable and keeps the remaining conditions stable. Record sensor configuration, rule version, clock reference, workload, and collection window. If several settings change together, attribute the result to the combined experiment instead of guessing which change caused it.</p> <p><strong>Endpoint detection and response (EDR)</strong> combines product-specific sensors and analysis. Direct API use, fewer child processes, or a changed memory layout does not establish the absence of other observable activity. Microsoft’s Sysmon documentation offers concrete examples of separate process, network, registry, and image-load observations. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Review the documented events"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/sysmon"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/sysmon" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Review the documented events</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Reputation is separate from correctness.</strong> Uploading an artifact to a scanning service is not a way to make it trusted. VirusTotal describes sharing submitted samples with its partners and community, so submission decisions require the artifact owner’s data-handling policy. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read how VirusTotal works"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.virustotal.com/docs/how-it-works"> <a href="https://docs.virustotal.com/docs/how-it-works" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read how VirusTotal works</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Claim</th> <th>Evidence problem</th> <th>Better conclusion</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>“No alert means unseen”</strong></td> <td>Collection and rule coverage unverified</td> <td>No alert observed in the stated window</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>“Longer sleep is safer”</strong></td> <td>Timing changed without measured detection</td> <td>Lower request frequency in this run</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>“A renamed process is trusted”</strong></td> <td>Name treated as provenance</td> <td>Identity and behavior still require review</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>“The profile passed lint”</strong></td> <td>Syntax treated as a security outcome</td> <td>Specified validation checks passed</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="work-a-comparison-case"> <a href="#work-a-comparison-case" title="Work a Comparison Case">Work a Comparison Case</a> <a href="#work-a-comparison-case" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Work a Comparison Case">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Illustrative scenario:</strong> two synthetic request runs each complete successfully. Run A produces an alert and Run B does not. Before Run B, the operator changes the user-agent and the analyst disables the relevant network-event collection rule.</p> <p><strong>Evaluate the conclusion:</strong> is the new user-agent responsible for the missing alert? Identify the confounding variable and write a justified next step. Keep the distinction between actual request behavior and available evidence explicit.</p> <p><strong>Expected reasoning:</strong> the comparison does not isolate the user-agent change. Collection changed as well, so the experiment cannot establish causation. Restore the agreed observation configuration, confirm it with a benign control, then repeat a bounded comparison with one changed variable.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Question: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Fixed environment and software versions: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Changed variable: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Baseline and comparison workloads: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Sensor health and collection configuration: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Expected observation and alert criteria: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Run IDs and timestamps: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Raw evidence locations: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Observed result and missing data: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Supported conclusion: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Follow-up or closure decision: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Your deliverable</strong> is a comparison record another reader would repeat using synthetic traffic. Include one alternative explanation for the result and the check which would distinguish it. Keep operational configuration details separate from unsupported claims about universal evasion.</p> <h2 id="watch-the-c2-lecture"> <a href="#watch-the-c2-lecture" title="Watch the C2 Lecture">Watch the C2 Lecture</a> <a href="#watch-the-c2-lecture" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Watch the C2 Lecture">#</a> </h2> <p>The <strong>Cobalt Strike Archive</strong> lecture introduces the profile language and communication design. Use it to identify the distinctions between an indicator, a transport dependency, and a claimed security outcome. Compare its examples with the evidence requirements in your experiment record.</p> <p><em>This historical 2019 lecture predates current releases. The documentation linked above takes precedence for current settings and supported behavior.</em></p> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Red Team Ops with Cobalt Strike (3 of 9): C2"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/Z8n9bIPAIao/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z8n9bIPAIao"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="Z8n9bIPAIao" videotitle="Red Team Ops with Cobalt Strike (3 of 9): C2" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z8n9bIPAIao" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Red Team Ops with Cobalt Strike (3 of 9): C2"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Red Team Ops with Cobalt Strike (3 of 9): C2", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/Z8n9bIPAIao\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z8n9bIPAIao", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Watch on YouTube:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Red Team Ops with Cobalt Strike (3 of 9): C2"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z8n9bIPAIao"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z8n9bIPAIao" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Red Team Ops with Cobalt Strike (3 of 9): C2</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="check-your-understanding"> <a href="#check-your-understanding" title="Check Your Understanding">Check Your Understanding</a> <a href="#check-your-understanding" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Check Your Understanding">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li><strong>Configuration:</strong> why does successful linting leave end-to-end behavior unproven?</li> <li><strong>Observation:</strong> why should every visibility claim name its sensor location?</li> <li><strong>Experiment:</strong> what invalidates the two-run comparison above?</li> <li><strong>Reporting:</strong> how would you phrase an absent alert without claiming invisibility?</li> </ol> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Configuration</strong></td> <td>The real route and its intermediaries were not exercised</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Observation</strong></td> <td>Encryption, endpoint context, and log configuration change the available view</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Experiment</strong></td> <td>Both the traffic field and collection configuration changed</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Reporting</strong></td> <td>Name the rule, collection state, window, and absence observed</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Evidence quality</strong> matters before any endpoint interaction as well. Continue to <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 8: Open-Source Intelligence"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/open-source-intelligence/"> <a href="/red-team-course/open-source-intelligence/" rel="follow me" >Module 8: Open-Source Intelligence</a> </span> to evaluate public information, freshness, and corroboration. item.title: CompTIA A+ (220-1202): Security
item.category: "CompTIA A+ Course" , "Security" , "Malware" , "Wireless Security" , "Windows Security" , "IT Support" , "CompTIA Certification" , "Help Desk" , "Social Engineering" , "Cybersecurity"
item.description: Master security for the CompTIA A+ 220-1202 Core 2 exam. Learn physical and logical security, Windows security settings, wireless protocols, malware, social engineering, and hardening.
item.content:encoded: <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Click Here to Return To the CompTIA A+ Course Page"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus-start/"> <a href="/a-plus-start/" rel="follow me" >Click Here to Return To the CompTIA A+ Course Page</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Security</strong> is <strong>28%</strong> of the <strong>CompTIA A+ 220-1202 Core 2</strong> exam, tied for the largest Core 2 domain. This module covers physical and logical security, Windows settings, wireless protocols, malware, social engineering, hardening, and data destruction. <em>Security knowledge protects every system you support, so master these controls.</em></p> <p>Security is everyone’s job, and the technician is the first line of defense. You lock down access, configure permissions, recognize attacks, and remove malware. This module builds the practical security skills the exam demands.</p> <h2 id="physical-and-logical-security"> <a href="#physical-and-logical-security" title="Physical and Logical Security">Physical and Logical Security</a> <a href="#physical-and-logical-security" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Physical and Logical Security">#</a> </h2> <p>You combine physical barriers with logical access controls.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Physical</th> <th>Logical</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Bollards, fences, mantraps</td> <td>Access Control Lists (ACLs)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Badge readers, key fobs</td> <td>Least privilege</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Biometrics (fingerprint, face)</td> <td>Zero Trust</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Locks, cameras, lighting</td> <td>Multifactor authentication (MFA)</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>MFA</strong> combines factors: something you <strong>know</strong> (password), something you <strong>have</strong> (token), and something you <strong>are</strong> (biometric). <strong>Least privilege</strong> gives each user only the access the job requires.</p> <h2 id="windows-security-settings"> <a href="#windows-security-settings" title="Windows Security Settings">Windows Security Settings</a> <a href="#windows-security-settings" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Windows Security Settings">#</a> </h2> <p>You harden Windows with built-in controls.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Microsoft Defender Antivirus</strong> blocks known and behavior-based malware.</li> <li><strong>Windows Defender Firewall</strong> filters network traffic.</li> <li><strong>NTFS vs share permissions</strong>: NTFS applies locally and over the network, share permissions apply only over the network. <em>The most restrictive of the two wins.</em></li> <li><strong>BitLocker</strong> encrypts the whole drive, while <strong>EFS</strong> encrypts individual files.</li> <li><strong>User Account Control (UAC)</strong> prompts before privileged actions.</li> </ul> <h2 id="wireless-security-protocols"> <a href="#wireless-security-protocols" title="Wireless Security Protocols">Wireless Security Protocols</a> <a href="#wireless-security-protocols" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Wireless Security Protocols">#</a> </h2> <p>You pick the strongest protocol the hardware supports.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Protocol</th> <th>Strength</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>WEP</strong></td> <td>Broken, never use</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>WPA2</strong></td> <td>AES encryption, still common</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>WPA3</strong></td> <td>Preferred current option where clients and access points support the selected mode</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Prefer a supported WPA3 mode with strong credentials and current device updates. WPA2 with AES-based CCMP remains a compatibility choice. Enterprise Wi-Fi commonly uses 802.1X with RADIUS. TACACS+ typically serves device administration. Kerberos issues tickets in domain environments, but is not a direct substitute for Wi-Fi authentication.</p> <h2 id="types-of-malware"> <a href="#types-of-malware" title="Types of Malware">Types of Malware</a> <a href="#types-of-malware" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Types of Malware">#</a> </h2> <p>You identify malware by its behavior.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Malware</th> <th>Behavior</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Virus</strong></td> <td>Attaches to files, spreads when run</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Trojan</strong></td> <td>Hides in a useful-looking program</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Ransomware</strong></td> <td>Encrypts data and demands payment</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Rootkit</strong></td> <td>Hides deep in the OS to evade detection</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Keylogger</strong></td> <td>Records keystrokes to steal credentials</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Cryptominer</strong></td> <td>Steals CPU/GPU cycles to mine coins</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Fileless</strong></td> <td>Runs in memory, leaves little on disk</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="social-engineering-and-threats"> <a href="#social-engineering-and-threats" title="Social Engineering and Threats">Social Engineering and Threats</a> <a href="#social-engineering-and-threats" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Social Engineering and Threats">#</a> </h2> <p>You recognize attacks that target people and systems.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Phishing</strong> uses fake emails to steal credentials, <strong>vishing</strong> uses voice calls, and <strong>smishing</strong> uses text messages.</li> <li><strong>Tailgating</strong> follows an authorized person through a secure door.</li> <li><strong>Shoulder surfing</strong> reads credentials over a shoulder.</li> <li><strong>DoS/DDoS</strong> floods a service to take it offline.</li> <li><strong>SQL injection</strong> and <strong>XSS</strong> attack vulnerable web applications.</li> </ul> <p>Strong, unique passwords blunt many of these attacks. Read <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="how to create strong passwords"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/how-to-create-strong-passwords/"> <a href="/articles/how-to-create-strong-passwords/" rel="follow me" >how to create strong passwords</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="malware-removal-and-hardening"> <a href="#malware-removal-and-hardening" title="Malware Removal and Hardening">Malware Removal and Hardening</a> <a href="#malware-removal-and-hardening" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Malware Removal and Hardening">#</a> </h2> <p>You follow the <strong>CompTIA seven-step malware removal process</strong>:</p> <ol> <li>Investigate and verify the malware symptoms.</li> <li>Quarantine the infected system.</li> <li>Disable System Restore (Windows).</li> <li>Remediate: update anti-malware and scan in safe mode.</li> <li>Schedule scans and run updates.</li> <li>Enable System Restore and create a restore point.</li> <li>Educate the end user.</li> </ol> <p>You <strong>harden workstations</strong> with data-at-rest encryption, strong password policies, account management, and by disabling unused services and AutoRun.</p> <h2 id="data-destruction"> <a href="#data-destruction" title="Data Destruction">Data Destruction</a> <a href="#data-destruction" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Data Destruction">#</a> </h2> <p>You destroy data so it cannot be recovered.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Method</th> <th>Type</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Drilling, shredding</strong></td> <td>Physical destruction</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Degaussing</strong></td> <td>Magnetic wipe of HDDs</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Secure erase / cryptographic erase</strong></td> <td>Software wipe</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Certified recycling</strong></td> <td>Documented disposal</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><em>Get a certificate of destruction when a third party handles regulated data.</em></p> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>Continue Core 2 with <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Software Troubleshooting"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus/software-troubleshooting-windows-apps-malware/"> <a href="/a-plus/software-troubleshooting-windows-apps-malware/" rel="follow me" >Software Troubleshooting</a> </span> for malware diagnosis, and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Operational Procedures"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus/operational-procedures-documentation-communication/"> <a href="/a-plus/operational-procedures-documentation-communication/" rel="follow me" >Operational Procedures</a> </span> for policy. Review <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Operating Systems"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus/operating-systems-windows-linux-macos/"> <a href="/a-plus/operating-systems-windows-linux-macos/" rel="follow me" >Operating Systems</a> </span> for Windows security tools. Return to the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CompTIA A+ Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus-start/"> <a href="/a-plus-start/" rel="follow me" >CompTIA A+ Course</a> </span> .</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 8: Open-Source Intelligence
item.description: Evaluate public sources, RDAP, DNS, certificate logs, and scan data. Build a traceable OSINT brief with worked examples and source-quality checks.
item.content:encoded: <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Open-source intelligence (OSINT)</strong> turns publicly available information into an answer to a defined question. Collection alone produces observations. Useful intelligence adds provenance, context, corroboration, uncertainty, and a decision the assessment team is authorized to make.</p> <p><em>Allow about 25 minutes, plus time to complete the evidence-ledger exercise. All organizations, observations, and assessment decisions in the worked case are fictional.</em></p> <h2 id="what-you-will-learn"> <a href="#what-you-will-learn" title="What You Will Learn">What You Will Learn</a> <a href="#what-you-will-learn" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What You Will Learn">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Distinguish</strong> a source observation from an inference and a confirmed finding.</li> <li><strong>Explain</strong> the limits of registration, DNS, certificate, and scan-index data.</li> <li><strong>Apply</strong> search operators and normalize a synthetic list of names.</li> <li><strong>Compare</strong> evidence freshness and independent corroboration.</li> <li><strong>Create</strong> a research brief which supports a bounded next action.</li> </ul> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Term</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Provenance</strong></td> <td>Where information originated and how you obtained it</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Observation</strong></td> <td>A specific item recorded from a source</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Inference</strong></td> <td>A conclusion drawn from one or more observations</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Corroboration</strong></td> <td>Additional evidence supporting or challenging a claim</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>RDAP</strong></td> <td>Registration Data Access Protocol for structured registration queries</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Certificate transparency</strong></td> <td>Public logging system for certificates and precertificates</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>ASN</strong></td> <td>Autonomous system number identifying a routing administration</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="start-with-a-question"> <a href="#start-with-a-question" title="Start With a Question">Start With a Question</a> <a href="#start-with-a-question" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Start With a Question">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A research question</strong> limits both collection and interpretation. “Which externally named services need ownership clarification before our approved scan?” produces a different collection plan from “Which public documents describe the organization’s remote-work policy?” Write the question before opening tools.</p> <p><strong>A finding</strong> needs a supported statement and its boundary. A search result mentioning a product does not prove the product is deployed now. A service banner naming a version does not establish the installed patch state or exploitability.</p> <p><strong>Decision relevance</strong> keeps the work focused. If a source does not change the answer or the next authorized action, collecting more of it adds handling work without improving the result. Maintain a short list of unresolved questions instead of an unlimited list of names.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Research question</th> <th>Useful evidence</th> <th>Premature conclusion</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Who manages a service?</strong></td> <td>Current inventory plus registration context</td> <td>Shared IP means shared ownership</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Was a name publicly disclosed?</strong></td> <td>Dated certificate or document record</td> <td>The service is live today</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Is a technology plausible?</strong></td> <td>Recent technical publication</td> <td>Every listed product is deployed</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="map-the-collection-path"> <a href="#map-the-collection-path" title="Map the Collection Path">Map the Collection Path</a> <a href="#map-the-collection-path" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Map the Collection Path">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Public availability</strong> describes access to information, not the visibility of collecting it. Reading a search index, loading the original website, and requesting a fresh service banner contact different systems. Search providers, APIs, resolvers, and websites have their own records of activity.</p> <p><strong>Passive relative to the target</strong> is a useful description if you define it. Querying an existing third-party dataset often avoids a new connection from you to the target service. Opening a result, fetching a linked image, or enabling an active tool module changes the collection path.</p> <p><strong>Collection records</strong> should therefore name the provider, account context where applicable, query, timestamp, and whether the tool initiates fresh target contact. An isolated browser profile separates work from personal sessions, but it does not guarantee anonymity or eliminate service-side logs.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/osint-observation-to-decision.webp", "caption": "Four connected boxes move from a research question to source observations, corroboration, and a bounded decision with uncertainty recorded", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-22 04:18:56.278339631 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b324.933432068", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-22 04:18:56.278339631 +0000 UTC m=+324.933432068"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/osint-observation-to-decision.webp" alt="Four connected boxes move from a research question to source observations, corroboration, and a bounded decision with uncertainty recorded"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Public information becomes useful intelligence through supported interpretation</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="use-search-operators-deliberately"> <a href="#use-search-operators-deliberately" title="Use Search Operators Deliberately">Use Search Operators Deliberately</a> <a href="#use-search-operators-deliberately" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Use Search Operators Deliberately">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Search operators</strong> narrow indexed results. Google documents quoted phrases, <strong><code>site:</code></strong>, <strong><code>filetype:</code></strong>, exclusions with <strong><code>-</code></strong>, and date filters such as <strong><code>after:</code></strong>. Operator support and interpretation differ between services, so check the search engine’s documentation. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read Google’s search guidance"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/2466433?hl=en"> <a href="https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/2466433?hl=en" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read Google’s search guidance</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Practice query design</strong> with the fictional examples below. The reserved example domain is a placeholder, so no matching results are expected. Replace it only with the domain selected for your authorized research task. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read IANA’s example-domain guidance"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.iana.org/help/example-domains"> <a href="https://www.iana.org/help/example-domains" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read IANA’s example-domain guidance</a> </span> .</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>site:example.com "remote access" </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>site:example.com filetype:pdf "annual report" </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>site:example.com "service status" -careers </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>site:example.com "migration" after:2025-01-01 </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Explain each filter</strong> before collecting results. The first limits the site and requests an exact phrase, the second adds a document type, the third excludes a word, and the fourth applies a date condition. A search-engine date filter is a retrieval aid, so verify the source’s own dates before interpreting freshness.</p> <p><strong>An empty result set</strong> is limited evidence. Indexing gaps, query wording, access restrictions, and removed pages affect the result. Record the query and its limits instead of concluding the organization has no remote-access service.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Source item</th> <th>Preserve</th> <th>Avoid assuming</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Search snippet</strong></td> <td>Query, retrieval time, and destination</td> <td>Snippet equals current page content</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Public document</strong></td> <td>Original file, date, and source URL</td> <td>Metadata proves current employment</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Job posting</strong></td> <td>Publication context and named requirements</td> <td>Every listed skill reflects production use</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="read-registration-records-carefully"> <a href="#read-registration-records-carefully" title="Read Registration Records Carefully">Read Registration Records Carefully</a> <a href="#read-registration-records-carefully" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Read Registration Records Carefully">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Domain registration data</strong> and <strong>IP-number registration data</strong> answer different questions. ICANN’s January 2025 transition made RDAP the definitive delivery mechanism for generic top-level-domain registration information in place of sunsetted WHOIS requirements. This does not mean every country-code domain or number-registry service follows an identical transition. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read ICANN’s announcement"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.icann.org/en/announcements/details/icann-update-launching-rdap-sunsetting-whois-27-01-2025-en"> <a href="https://www.icann.org/en/announcements/details/icann-update-launching-rdap-sunsetting-whois-27-01-2025-en" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read ICANN’s announcement</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Regional Internet Registries</strong> provide number-resource information. ARIN’s RDAP documentation covers queries for networks, autonomous systems, and related entities. A returned record describes registration relationships, not necessarily the current application operator using an address. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read ARIN’s RDAP guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.arin.net/resources/registry/whois/rdap/"> <a href="https://www.arin.net/resources/registry/whois/rdap/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read ARIN’s RDAP guide</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Scope remains a separate record.</strong> A cloud provider’s allocation does not authorize testing every tenant within it. Conversely, a customer-operated service on provider address space is not automatically excluded if the agreed scope and applicable provider conditions explicitly include it.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Record</th> <th>Supports</th> <th>Does not establish</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Domain RDAP</strong></td> <td>Registration details exposed by the service</td> <td>Current technical administrator in every case</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Network RDAP</strong></td> <td>Number-resource registration context</td> <td>Application ownership or assessment permission</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Approved asset register</strong></td> <td>Named assessment targets and constraints</td> <td>Current network state without verification</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="interpret-dns-relationships"> <a href="#interpret-dns-relationships" title="Interpret DNS Relationships">Interpret DNS Relationships</a> <a href="#interpret-dns-relationships" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Interpret DNS Relationships">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>DNS names</strong> are not a one-to-one inventory of machines. Multiple names resolve to one service, one name resolves to multiple addresses, and an alias refers to another name. Delegation also separates a parent zone from a child zone. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the DNS concepts specification"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1034.html"> <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1034.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the DNS concepts specification</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Record types</strong> provide different evidence. Address records associate names with addresses, MX records identify mail exchangers, NS records describe authoritative servers, and TXT records carry text with application-specific meaning. A TXT value mentioning a provider is a lead about configuration, not proof every provider feature is active.</p> <p><strong>AXFR</strong> transfers the contents of a DNS zone under the protocol’s rules. It is not inherently a misconfiguration and does not return every host in an entire delegated domain tree. Whether a requester is permitted to receive a zone is an authorization and configuration question. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the AXFR specification"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5936.html"> <a href="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5936.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the AXFR specification</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Observation</th> <th>Reasonable interpretation</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Two names, one address</strong></td> <td>Shared resolution result, with service identity still unresolved</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Alias to a provider name</strong></td> <td>A DNS dependency worth validating with the asset owner</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Child-zone delegation</strong></td> <td>Separate authoritative data below the delegation point</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>No public answer</strong></td> <td>No answer from this query context, not proof no internal service exists</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="understand-certificate-transparency"> <a href="#understand-certificate-transparency" title="Understand Certificate Transparency">Understand Certificate Transparency</a> <a href="#understand-certificate-transparency" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Understand Certificate Transparency">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Certificate transparency (CT)</strong> makes submitted certificates and precertificates auditable through public logs. It supports monitoring issuance in the public web PKI ecosystem. It is not a complete database of every certificate, private PKI, or service endpoint. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read how CT works"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://certificate.transparency.dev/howctworks/"> <a href="https://certificate.transparency.dev/howctworks/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read how CT works</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Certificate names</strong> provide historical naming evidence. A certificate containing <strong><code>portal.example.com</code></strong> suggests the name mattered to its requester at issuance, but does not prove a service is currently reachable there. A wildcard such as <strong><code>*.example.com</code></strong> does not enumerate all individual names covered by its pattern.</p> <p><strong>Log duplicates</strong> also need interpretation. One certificate submitted to several logs is not several independently observed servers. Preserve the certificate identity and source relationships when counting evidence.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Certificate evidence</th> <th>Supported statement</th> <th>Unsupported leap</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Named entry</strong></td> <td>A name appears in the recorded certificate</td> <td>A live vulnerable server exists</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Wildcard entry</strong></td> <td>A wildcard name was included</td> <td>Every possible subdomain is deployed</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Expired certificate</strong></td> <td>Historical issuance evidence exists</td> <td>The associated service remains active</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="treat-scan-data-as-historical"> <a href="#treat-scan-data-as-historical" title="Treat Scan Data as Historical">Treat Scan Data as Historical</a> <a href="#treat-scan-data-as-historical" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Treat Scan Data as Historical">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Shodan records</strong> describe observations made by Shodan’s collection systems. Their value comes from the captured service information and associated timestamps. A stored banner is not a new measurement from your current vantage point.</p> <p><strong>Timeframes matter.</strong> Shodan documents different historical windows across its services, with its principal search interfaces presenting recent banner observations within a defined rolling window. Read the record’s collection timestamp and the interface’s documented behavior before describing a result as current. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read Shodan’s data-timeframe documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://help.shodan.io/mastery/data_timeline"> <a href="https://help.shodan.io/mastery/data_timeline" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read Shodan’s data-timeframe documentation</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Service identity needs corroboration.</strong> An address might be reassigned, a reverse proxy might answer on behalf of several applications, or a banner might conceal the underlying version. A result is a lead for the approved validation plan, not automatic proof of ownership or vulnerability.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Compare these times</th> <th>Why they differ</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Observed at</strong></td> <td>When the provider collected the source observation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Retrieved at</strong></td> <td>When you obtained the record</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Published at</strong></td> <td>When a page or report became available</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Valid for decision</strong></td> <td>Your stated freshness requirement for the research question</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="choose-automation-by-behavior"> <a href="#choose-automation-by-behavior" title="Choose Automation by Behavior">Choose Automation by Behavior</a> <a href="#choose-automation-by-behavior" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Choose Automation by Behavior">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>SpiderFoot</strong> provides modules for gathering and correlating information from multiple sources. Module selection, API access, and collection behavior affect what a run does. Review the selected modules before assuming a tool labeled “OSINT” only reads existing third-party records. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the project documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/smicallef/spiderfoot"> <a href="https://github.com/smicallef/spiderfoot" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the project documentation</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Tool choice</strong> follows the question. A graph helps review relationships, a document parser extracts metadata, and a search service locates indexed material. None of those operations independently verifies the meaning of the resulting relationship.</p> <p><strong>Rate and data limits</strong> belong in the collection plan. Record provider limits, allowed input types, and the necessary output fields before automation. Avoid expanding from an approved domain investigation into unrelated personal profiles because a module offers more pivots.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Need</th> <th>Appropriate tool behavior</th> <th>Review requirement</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Find published material</strong></td> <td>Search an index</td> <td>Verify the original source</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Correlate names</strong></td> <td>Normalize and graph records</td> <td>Preserve provenance and duplicates</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Extract document metadata</strong></td> <td>Parse a saved public file</td> <td>Distinguish metadata from verified identity</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Map exposure leads</strong></td> <td>Read existing service observations</td> <td>Check age, ownership, and scope</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="normalize-without-inventing-evidence"> <a href="#normalize-without-inventing-evidence" title="Normalize Without Inventing Evidence">Normalize Without Inventing Evidence</a> <a href="#normalize-without-inventing-evidence" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Normalize Without Inventing Evidence">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Normalization</strong> removes superficial differences while preserving the original observations. Lowercasing a DNS name and removing its final root dot helps compare names. Treat a certificate wildcard separately instead of converting it into an invented host.</p> <p><strong>Run this local example</strong> with Python 3. It performs no network requests and writes no files. The output separates exact names from a wildcard certificate pattern.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-python" data-lang="python"><span style="display:flex;"><span>observations <span style="color:#f92672">=</span> [ </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#e6db74">"Portal.Example.com."</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#e6db74">"portal.example.com"</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#e6db74">"*.example.com"</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#e6db74">"status.example.com"</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>] </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>names <span style="color:#f92672">=</span> set() </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>wildcards <span style="color:#f92672">=</span> set() </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#66d9ef">for</span> original <span style="color:#f92672">in</span> observations: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> normalized <span style="color:#f92672">=</span> original<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>lower()<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>rstrip(<span style="color:#e6db74">"."</span>) </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#66d9ef">if</span> normalized<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>startswith(<span style="color:#e6db74">"*."</span>): </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> wildcards<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>add(normalized) </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#66d9ef">else</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> names<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>add(normalized) </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>print(<span style="color:#e6db74">"Exact names:"</span>, <span style="color:#e6db74">", "</span><span style="color:#f92672">.</span>join(sorted(names))) </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>print(<span style="color:#e6db74">"Wildcard patterns:"</span>, <span style="color:#e6db74">", "</span><span style="color:#f92672">.</span>join(sorted(wildcards))) </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Expected output</strong> contains two distinct exact names and one wildcard pattern. The duplicate portal spelling collapses into one name, but your evidence ledger should retain both original source rows. Deduplication for counting is different from deleting provenance.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Exact names: portal.example.com, status.example.com </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Wildcard patterns: *.example.com </span></span></code></pre></div><h2 id="work-an-evidence-case"> <a href="#work-an-evidence-case" title="Work an Evidence Case">Work an Evidence Case</a> <a href="#work-an-evidence-case" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Work an Evidence Case">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Illustrative case:</strong> an assessment permits research about the fictional Example organization. The active-scan list contains <strong><code>status.example.com</code></strong> only. You collect the following synthetic records while investigating whether a second portal needs ownership review.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Record</th> <th>Observation</th> <th>Collection context</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>A</strong></td> <td>Certificate names portal.example.com</td> <td>Issued 18 months before review</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>B</strong></td> <td>Blog repeats the certificate name</td> <td>Links directly to record A</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>C</strong></td> <td>Archived banner identifies a portal</td> <td>Provider observed it 24 days earlier</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>D</strong></td> <td>Owner inventory lists a retired portal</td> <td>Inventory updated this week</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Analyze the evidence:</strong> decide whether A and B independently corroborate the portal’s current state. Identify the newest relevant record and the unresolved relationship between C and D. Then decide whether these records authorize scanning the portal.</p> <p><strong>Expected reasoning:</strong> B repeats A, so they share one underlying source. D is the newest inventory statement, while C reflects an earlier external observation. The apparent conflict might represent a retirement after collection, a stale inventory, or a mistaken service association.</p> <p><strong>The next action</strong> is ownership clarification through the assessment’s agreed contact. The evidence supports asking about an unresolved exposure lead, not adding the portal to the scan list. A useful brief names the exact conflict and requests the smallest confirmation needed.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Claim ID: OSINT-PORTAL-01 </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Question: Does the historical portal need approved exposure validation? </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Supported facts: Certificate name, dated banner, retirement inventory entry </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Shared sources: B derives from A </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Uncertainty: Current state and relationship between C and D </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Scope status: Not on the approved active-scan list </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Next action: Ask the asset owner to reconcile the records </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Evidence locations: A, B, C, D with source URLs and timestamps </span></span></code></pre></div><h2 id="assess-source-quality"> <a href="#assess-source-quality" title="Assess Source Quality">Assess Source Quality</a> <a href="#assess-source-quality" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Assess Source Quality">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Independent corroboration</strong> depends on origin, not website count. Ten articles repeating one press release still share a source. Follow citations backward and retain both the originating item and the later interpretation when the distinction matters.</p> <p><strong>Visual evidence</strong> also needs context. An image or video supports claims about what it depicts only after its origin, location, time, and relevant features are examined. Bellingcat’s verification examples demonstrate checking an item’s claimed context against other evidence. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read its social-media verification guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.bellingcat.com/resources/2021/11/01/a-beginners-guide-to-social-media-verification/"> <a href="https://www.bellingcat.com/resources/2021/11/01/a-beginners-guide-to-social-media-verification/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read its social-media verification guide</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Confidence</strong> should explain reasoning rather than imply a calculated probability without a model. Use terms such as “supported historical observation,” “current owner confirmation,” and “unverified lead.” State what new evidence would change the conclusion.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Quality question</th> <th>Useful check</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Origin</strong></td> <td>Locate the earliest identifiable source</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Freshness</strong></td> <td>Compare collection time with the decision window</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Independence</strong></td> <td>Trace whether sources copy one another</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Contradiction</strong></td> <td>Record evidence challenging the preferred explanation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Relevance</strong></td> <td>Connect the observation to the research question</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="watch-the-toolkit-introduction"> <a href="#watch-the-toolkit-introduction" title="Watch the Toolkit Introduction">Watch the Toolkit Introduction</a> <a href="#watch-the-toolkit-introduction" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Watch the Toolkit Introduction">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Bellingcat’s toolkit presentation</strong> introduces resources for open-source investigation. Use it to choose a method for a defined question rather than collecting a long list of unrelated tools. For one demonstrated resource, write down its input, output, and verification limits.</p> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Presenting: The Bellingcat Online Open Source Investigations Toolkit"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/-Y3GQ6mSGqM/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Y3GQ6mSGqM"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="-Y3GQ6mSGqM" videotitle="Presenting: The Bellingcat Online Open Source Investigations Toolkit" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Y3GQ6mSGqM" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Presenting: The Bellingcat Online Open Source Investigations Toolkit"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Presenting: The Bellingcat Online Open Source Investigations Toolkit", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/-Y3GQ6mSGqM\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Y3GQ6mSGqM", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Watch on YouTube:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Presenting: The Bellingcat Online Open Source Investigations Toolkit"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Y3GQ6mSGqM"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Y3GQ6mSGqM" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Presenting: The Bellingcat Online Open Source Investigations Toolkit</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="create-your-research-brief"> <a href="#create-your-research-brief" title="Create Your Research Brief">Create Your Research Brief</a> <a href="#create-your-research-brief" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create Your Research Brief">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Build a one-page brief</strong> from five synthetic observations. Include one duplicate source, one stale record, one conflicting record, and one item irrelevant to the research question. Explain which items affect the decision and which do not.</p> <p><strong>Preserve a minimal evidence package</strong> with source URLs, retrieval times, original records where appropriate, and the relevant excerpts. Avoid unnecessary personal information or secrets. If a public source appears to expose a credential, follow the agreed reporting process rather than treating availability as permission to use it.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Brief section</th> <th>Required content</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Question and scope</strong></td> <td>What the research should answer and permitted next actions</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Evidence</strong></td> <td>Observations with provenance and timestamps</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Analysis</strong></td> <td>Corroboration, contradictions, and source dependencies</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Conclusion</strong></td> <td>Supported answer and explicit uncertainty</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Next action</strong></td> <td>Owner, requested clarification, or approved validation</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Evaluate your brief</strong> by asking another reader to reconstruct the reasoning from the preserved evidence. They should distinguish what you observed, what you inferred, and what remains unresolved. A persuasive paragraph without traceable sources is not a finished intelligence product.</p> <h2 id="check-your-understanding"> <a href="#check-your-understanding" title="Check Your Understanding">Check Your Understanding</a> <a href="#check-your-understanding" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Check Your Understanding">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li><strong>Collection:</strong> does public availability guarantee an unobserved lookup?</li> <li><strong>Registration:</strong> why is an IP allocation record insufficient to establish scan scope?</li> <li><strong>Certificates:</strong> does a wildcard enumerate deployed hostnames?</li> <li><strong>Corroboration:</strong> do two websites repeating one certificate entry count as independent evidence?</li> <li><strong>Freshness:</strong> which timestamp describes when a scan provider observed a banner?</li> </ol> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Collection</strong></td> <td>Providers and contacted systems have their own observation paths</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Registration</strong></td> <td>Resource registration and assessment authorization are separate facts</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Certificates</strong></td> <td>A wildcard is a naming pattern, not a host list</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Corroboration</strong></td> <td>Shared origin limits independence</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Freshness</strong></td> <td>The observation timestamp, distinct from your retrieval time</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Active reconnaissance</strong> tests approved questions against current services. Continue to <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 9: Active Reconnaissance and Scanning"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/active-reconnaissance-and-scanning/"> <a href="/red-team-course/active-reconnaissance-and-scanning/" rel="follow me" >Module 9: Active Reconnaissance and Scanning</a> </span> with a bounded target list and unresolved questions. Return to the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Red Team Course hub"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Red Team Course hub</a> </span> for the full sequence.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: CompTIA A+ (220-1202): Software Troubleshooting
item.category: "CompTIA A+ Course" , "Software Troubleshooting" , "Malware Removal" , "Windows" , "Mobile OS" , "IT Support" , "CompTIA Certification" , "Help Desk" , "Diagnostics" , "IT Fundamentals"
item.description: Master software troubleshooting for the CompTIA A+ 220-1202 Core 2 exam. Diagnose Windows OS issues, mobile OS and application problems, security symptoms, and malware removal.
item.content:encoded: <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Click Here to Return To the CompTIA A+ Course Page"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus-start/"> <a href="/a-plus-start/" rel="follow me" >Click Here to Return To the CompTIA A+ Course Page</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Software Troubleshooting</strong> is <strong>23%</strong> of the <strong>CompTIA A+ 220-1202 Core 2</strong> exam.
