This module covers Windows OS issues, mobile OS and application problems, security symptoms, and malware removal. <em>Pair this domain with the Core 1 troubleshooting methodology because the same process applies to software.</em></p> <p>Software problems frustrate users and fill the ticket queue. You read the symptoms, match them to a cause, and apply the fix that solves the problem without losing data. This module covers the software faults you will see most.</p> <h2 id="windows-os-troubleshooting"> <a href="#windows-os-troubleshooting" title="Windows OS Troubleshooting">Windows OS Troubleshooting</a> <a href="#windows-os-troubleshooting" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Windows OS Troubleshooting">#</a> </h2> <p>You diagnose the common Windows failures.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Symptom</th> <th>Likely cause</th> <th>Fix</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>BSOD / stop error</strong></td> <td>Bad driver, RAM, or hardware</td> <td>Check driver, run memory test</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Boot failure</strong></td> <td>Corrupt boot files</td> <td>Startup Repair, <code>bootrec</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Frequent shutdowns</strong></td> <td>Overheating or PSU</td> <td>Check temps and power</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Services not starting</strong></td> <td>Dependency or corruption</td> <td>Check Services and Event Viewer</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Slow performance</strong></td> <td>Startup bloat, low disk, malware</td> <td>Trim startup, free space, scan</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Time drift</strong></td> <td>Dead CMOS battery or NTP</td> <td>Replace battery, sync time</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>You repair core files from the command line:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>sfc /scannow <span style="color:#75715e"># Repair system files</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth <span style="color:#75715e"># Repair the component store</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>chkdsk C: /f /r <span style="color:#75715e"># Fix filesystem and recover sectors</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><h2 id="mobile-os-and-application-issues"> <a href="#mobile-os-and-application-issues" title="Mobile OS and Application Issues">Mobile OS and Application Issues</a> <a href="#mobile-os-and-application-issues" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Mobile OS and Application Issues">#</a> </h2> <p>You fix phones and tablets that misbehave.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Apps failing to launch or crashing</strong> call for an update, cache clear, or reinstall.</li> <li><strong>Battery drain</strong> points to a rogue app, poor signal, or background activity.</li> <li><strong>Random reboots</strong> suggest an OS bug, a bad update, or failing hardware.</li> <li><strong>Slow performance</strong> traces to low storage or too many background apps.</li> <li><strong>Connectivity problems</strong> need a check of Wi-Fi, cellular, Bluetooth, and airplane mode.</li> </ul> <h2 id="mobile-security-issues"> <a href="#mobile-security-issues" title="Mobile Security Issues">Mobile Security Issues</a> <a href="#mobile-security-issues" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Mobile Security Issues">#</a> </h2> <p>You spot signs that a mobile device is compromised.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Symptom</th> <th>Concern</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Jailbreak / root detected</strong></td> <td>Security controls bypassed</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>High network traffic</strong></td> <td>Data exfiltration or malware</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Fake security warnings</strong></td> <td>Scareware or a malicious app</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Unexpected app permissions</strong></td> <td>Spyware or overreaching app</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Unusual battery drain</strong></td> <td>Hidden background activity</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><em>Removing root or jailbreak and reinstalling from a clean image restores trust.</em></p> <h2 id="pc-security-symptoms"> <a href="#pc-security-symptoms" title="PC Security Symptoms">PC Security Symptoms</a> <a href="#pc-security-symptoms" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="PC Security Symptoms">#</a> </h2> <p>You recognize a compromised desktop.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Desktop alerts and fake antivirus warnings</strong> are scareware.</li> <li><strong>Altered or renamed files</strong> can signal ransomware.</li> <li><strong>Browser redirection</strong> and <strong>frequent pop-ups</strong> point to adware or a hijacked browser.</li> <li><strong>Certificate warnings</strong> can indicate a man-in-the-middle attack.</li> <li><strong>New, unknown toolbars or extensions</strong> are often malicious.</li> </ul> <p>A privacy-focused browser reduces this risk. See <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="the best privacy browsers"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/best-privacy-browsers-librewolf-brave-firefox-tor/"> <a href="/articles/best-privacy-browsers-librewolf-brave-firefox-tor/" rel="follow me" >the best privacy browsers</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="malware-removal-techniques"> <a href="#malware-removal-techniques" title="Malware Removal Techniques">Malware Removal Techniques</a> <a href="#malware-removal-techniques" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Malware Removal Techniques">#</a> </h2> <p>You remove stubborn malware with the right tools.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Safe Mode</strong> loads fewer drivers and services. It helps isolate some faults and malware interference, but it does not guarantee a clean scan.</li> <li><strong>Preinstallation environments (WinPE)</strong> scan offline before Windows loads.</li> <li><strong>Reimaging</strong> wipes and restores a clean OS image when removal fails.</li> <li><strong>System Restore</strong> rolls back to a clean point, <em>though sophisticated malware can survive it</em>.</li> </ul> <p>Follow the full seven-step process detailed in the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Security module"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus/security-threats-vulnerabilities-best-practices/"> <a href="/a-plus/security-threats-vulnerabilities-best-practices/" rel="follow me" >Security module</a> </span> . Verify file integrity after cleanup using <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="how to get hashes of files in Windows"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/guides/how-to-get-hashes-of-files-in-windows/"> <a href="/guides/how-to-get-hashes-of-files-in-windows/" rel="follow me" >how to get hashes of files in Windows</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>Finish Core 2 with <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Operational Procedures"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus/operational-procedures-documentation-communication/"> <a href="/a-plus/operational-procedures-documentation-communication/" rel="follow me" >Operational Procedures</a> </span> . Review the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Security"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus/security-threats-vulnerabilities-best-practices/"> <a href="/a-plus/security-threats-vulnerabilities-best-practices/" rel="follow me" >Security</a> </span> module for malware types and the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Operating Systems"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus/operating-systems-windows-linux-macos/"> <a href="/a-plus/operating-systems-windows-linux-macos/" rel="follow me" >Operating Systems</a> </span> module for repair tools. Return to the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CompTIA A+ Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus-start/"> <a href="/a-plus-start/" rel="follow me" >CompTIA A+ Course</a> </span> and take the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CompTIA A+ Practice Test"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus-practice-test/"> <a href="/a-plus-practice-test/" rel="follow me" >CompTIA A+ Practice Test</a> </span> .</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 9: Active Reconnaissance and Scanning
item.description: Interpret Nmap port states, scan methods, and vantage points through a loopback exercise, segmentation case, and evidence-based scan plan.
item.content:encoded: <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Active reconnaissance</strong> sends requests to a system to answer a defined question about its current behavior. A scan result describes what the scanner observed from a particular location at a particular time. It becomes useful when you preserve the method, interpret the limits, and connect the result to an approved next action.</p> <p><em>Allow about 20 minutes, plus time for the loopback exercise. The exercise uses one port on your own machine.</em></p> <h2 id="what-you-will-learn"> <a href="#what-you-will-learn" title="What You Will Learn">What You Will Learn</a> <a href="#what-you-will-learn" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What You Will Learn">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Distinguish</strong> host discovery, port state, service identification, and vulnerability validation.</li> <li><strong>Explain</strong> the differences between TCP SYN and connect scans.</li> <li><strong>Run</strong> a bounded local scan and preserve its output.</li> <li><strong>Analyze</strong> conflicting observations from different vantage points.</li> <li><strong>Create</strong> a scan plan with evidence requirements and stopping conditions.</li> </ul> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Term</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Vantage point</strong></td> <td>Network location and routing context of the observer</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Host discovery</strong></td> <td>Probes used to identify responsive addresses</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Port scan</strong></td> <td>Probes used to classify transport endpoints</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Service identification</strong></td> <td>Evidence about the application using an endpoint</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Deconfliction</strong></td> <td>Coordination which distinguishes assessment activity from other events</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Scan manifest</strong></td> <td>Record of targets, options, timing, source, and purpose</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="ask-a-bounded-question"> <a href="#ask-a-bounded-question" title="Ask a Bounded Question">Ask a Bounded Question</a> <a href="#ask-a-bounded-question" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Ask a Bounded Question">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Start with the decision</strong>. “Does the training web service accept TCP connections on its assigned port?” needs less probing than a complete asset inventory. Define the target, transport, port, and allowed method before choosing options.</p> <p><strong>Scope and ownership</strong> remain separate from reachability. A name resolving to an address does not expand your authorization to every service or tenant using it. Carry unresolved ownership questions from <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 8"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/open-source-intelligence/"> <a href="/red-team-course/open-source-intelligence/" rel="follow me" >Module 8</a> </span> into the scan plan instead of resolving them through speculative probes.</p> <p><strong>Source selection</strong> determines which network boundary the scan tests. Use the agreed assessment source and record its identity. A redirector is a forwarding role, not a requirement for every scan, and a disposable source still creates costs, records, and coordination obligations.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Smallest relevant observation</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Is this port reachable?</strong></td> <td>Transport response from the approved source</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Which service answers?</strong></td> <td>Authorized application-level response</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Does a control block access?</strong></td> <td>Response plus control-side evidence</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Is a vulnerability present?</strong></td> <td>Separate validated conditions beyond a port label</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="understand-scan-states"> <a href="#understand-scan-states" title="Understand Scan States">Understand Scan States</a> <a href="#understand-scan-states" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Understand Scan States">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Nmap states</strong> describe the scanner’s interpretation of responses. An <strong>open</strong> TCP port accepts connections, while a <strong>closed</strong> port responds without a listening service. <strong>Filtered</strong> means the scan lacks enough access to determine whether the port is open. These are observations rather than permanent properties of a machine. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read Nmap’s port-state definitions"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://nmap.org/book/man-port-scanning-basics.html"> <a href="https://nmap.org/book/man-port-scanning-basics.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read Nmap’s port-state definitions</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Combined states</strong>, such as <strong><code>open|filtered</code></strong>, preserve ambiguity. Do not convert them into confirmed open services when building a report. The permitted interpretation depends on the scan method and returned evidence.</p> <p><strong>Vantage point matters.</strong> A service reachable from a management subnet might be filtered from a guest subnet. Those results are compatible with a working segmentation policy, so retain both rather than selecting whichever looks more conclusive.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/scan-vantage-response-interpretation.webp", "caption": "Four boxes connect a bounded scan question, source vantage point, observed response, and a conclusion constrained by the evidence", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-22 04:18:56.283448093 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b324.938540551", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-22 04:18:56.283448093 +0000 UTC m=+324.938540551"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/scan-vantage-response-interpretation.webp" alt="Four boxes connect a bounded scan question, source vantage point, observed response, and a conclusion constrained by the evidence"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>The scan’s location and method are part of the result</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="compare-tcp-scan-methods"> <a href="#compare-tcp-scan-methods" title="Compare TCP Scan Methods">Compare TCP Scan Methods</a> <a href="#compare-tcp-scan-methods" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Compare TCP Scan Methods">#</a> </h2> <p>A <strong>TCP connect scan</strong>, selected with <strong><code>-sT</code></strong>, asks the operating system to establish a connection. It completes the TCP handshake when an open service accepts it. It does not require the raw-packet privileges used by a SYN scan. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read Nmap’s connect-scan documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://nmap.org/book/scan-methods-connect-scan.html"> <a href="https://nmap.org/book/scan-methods-connect-scan.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read Nmap’s connect-scan documentation</a> </span> .</p> <p>A <strong>SYN scan</strong>, selected with <strong><code>-sS</code></strong>, examines responses without completing the connection in the same way. Both methods remain observable to suitable sensors. Completing a handshake is insufficient evidence of normal application use or avoided detection.</p> <p><strong>Method choice</strong> follows privileges, platform support, the question, and the permitted assessment behavior. Nmap’s own documentation describes the greater likelihood of application-side records from connect scans. Avoid teaching <strong><code>-sT</code></strong> as universally quieter than <strong><code>-sS</code></strong>.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Method</th> <th>Connection behavior</th> <th>Interpretation limit</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>TCP connect</strong></td> <td>Uses the operating system’s connection API</td> <td>Successful handshake proves no application operation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>TCP SYN</strong></td> <td>Evaluates raw TCP responses</td> <td>Half-open does not mean unobserved</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Service probes</strong></td> <td>Add application-specific requests</td> <td>More interaction than a port-state check</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="separate-discovery-from-scanning"> <a href="#separate-discovery-from-scanning" title="Separate Discovery From Scanning">Separate Discovery From Scanning</a> <a href="#separate-discovery-from-scanning" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Separate Discovery From Scanning">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Host discovery</strong> is a preliminary question about responsive addresses. Nmap supports several probe types, so it is broader than an ICMP echo request. A blocked discovery probe does not establish the unreachability of every service on the address. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the host-discovery reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://nmap.org/book/man-host-discovery.html"> <a href="https://nmap.org/book/man-host-discovery.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the host-discovery reference</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong><code>-Pn</code></strong> skips ordinary host discovery and treats specified targets as available for the requested scan. It is not a stealth option and does not make a failed route work. On some local network paths, link-layer resolution still takes place.</p> <p><strong>Port selection</strong> should reflect the question. The <strong><code>-p</code></strong> option selects explicit ports, while an ordinary default scan covers Nmap’s selected common ports rather than every possible port. Record the exact selection so readers understand what the scan omitted. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the port-specification reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://nmap.org/book/man-port-specification.html"> <a href="https://nmap.org/book/man-port-specification.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the port-specification reference</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Observation</th> <th>Insufficient conclusion</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>No discovery reply</strong></td> <td>Every service is unavailable</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>One selected port is closed</strong></td> <td>The host has no listening applications</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Default scan finds nothing</strong></td> <td>All TCP and UDP ports were tested</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>TCP connection succeeds</strong></td> <td>Authentication and application access will succeed</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="run-a-loopback-exercise"> <a href="#run-a-loopback-exercise" title="Run a Loopback Exercise">Run a Loopback Exercise</a> <a href="#run-a-loopback-exercise" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Run a Loopback Exercise">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Prepare a temporary service</strong> with Python 3 in a terminal. The server binds only to <strong><code>127.0.0.1</code></strong>, and <strong><code>--directory</code></strong> points to a newly created empty folder. This keeps the example’s service off external interfaces and away from your working files. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read Python’s demonstration-server documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.server.html"> <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.server.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read Python’s demonstration-server documentation</a> </span> .</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>scan_lab_dir<span style="color:#f92672">=</span><span style="color:#66d9ef">$(</span>mktemp -d<span style="color:#66d9ef">)</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>python3 -m http.server <span style="color:#ae81ff">8765</span> --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$scan_lab_dir<span style="color:#e6db74">"</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Use a second terminal</strong> with Nmap installed to scan the one local port. First create a temporary results directory so repeated exercises do not overwrite previous evidence. The command requests a TCP connect scan, skips DNS lookups and host discovery, and saves XML plus readable output.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>scan_results_dir<span style="color:#f92672">=</span><span style="color:#66d9ef">$(</span>mktemp -d<span style="color:#66d9ef">)</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>nmap -sT -Pn -n -p <span style="color:#ae81ff">8765</span> --reason <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -oX <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$scan_results_dir<span style="color:#e6db74">/listening.xml"</span> <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -oN <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$scan_results_dir<span style="color:#e6db74">/listening.nmap"</span> <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> 127.0.0.1 </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Flag meanings:</strong> <strong><code>-sT</code></strong> selects connect scanning, <strong><code>-Pn</code></strong> skips ordinary discovery, <strong><code>-n</code></strong> disables DNS resolution, and <strong><code>-p 8765</code></strong> restricts the port list. <strong><code>--reason</code></strong> includes the basis for the state classification. <strong><code>-oX</code></strong> and <strong><code>-oN</code></strong> name the XML and readable output files. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read Nmap’s output reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://nmap.org/book/man-output.html"> <a href="https://nmap.org/book/man-output.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read Nmap’s output reference</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Expected result:</strong> port <strong><code>8765/tcp</code></strong> appears open while the local server is listening. The displayed service name is not proof Python’s HTTP server was identified. No version-detection option was requested.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Exercise phase</th> <th>Expected TCP state</th> <th>Required condition</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Server running</strong></td> <td>Open</td> <td>Server bound successfully to the chosen port</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Server stopped</strong></td> <td>Closed</td> <td>No replacement listener or filtering interference</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Stop the server</strong> with <strong>Ctrl+C</strong> in its terminal. Repeat the scan from the second terminal using different output filenames. Leave the source, target, options, and port unchanged so the listener state is the intended difference.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>nmap -sT -Pn -n -p <span style="color:#ae81ff">8765</span> --reason <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -oX <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$scan_results_dir<span style="color:#e6db74">/stopped.xml"</span> <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -oN <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$scan_results_dir<span style="color:#e6db74">/stopped.nmap"</span> <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> 127.0.0.1 </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Compare your observations</strong> with the expected states. If the port remains open, check for another listener or an unsuccessful shutdown. If the initial scan was closed, check whether the server started and whether both commands used the same port.</p> <p><strong>Preserve the evidence</strong> before removing the disposable directories. Print their paths with <strong><code>printf '%s\n' "$scan_lab_dir"</code></strong> and <strong><code>printf '%s\n' "$scan_results_dir"</code></strong> in the respective shells. This exercise demonstrates a controlled state change, not the behavior of a remote firewall.</p> <h2 id="identify-services-separately"> <a href="#identify-services-separately" title="Identify Services Separately">Identify Services Separately</a> <a href="#identify-services-separately" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Identify Services Separately">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A port-number label</strong> is a naming convention, not a measured application identity. A service on port 443 is not automatically HTTPS, and an HTTP service is not restricted to port 80. Nmap’s <strong><code>-sV</code></strong> option performs additional probes to identify services and versions. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the service-detection reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://nmap.org/book/man-version-detection.html"> <a href="https://nmap.org/book/man-version-detection.html" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the service-detection reference</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Additional probes</strong> change the test. A transport check, a banner request, an authenticated application test, and a vulnerability test have different prerequisites and effects. Keep them as separately justified actions rather than adding every available option to the initial command.</p> <p><strong>Version strings</strong> also need context. Reverse proxies, customized banners, vendor backports, and incomplete fingerprints complicate interpretation. A suspected version warrants an evidence-based follow-up, not an automatic vulnerability claim.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Evidence</th> <th>What to report</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Port-state result</strong></td> <td>Endpoint, method, state, reason, and vantage</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Application response</strong></td> <td>Protocol behavior and observed identifying fields</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Version inference</strong></td> <td>Matched evidence and confidence limits</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Validated finding</strong></td> <td>Specific conditions, supported impact, and reproduction boundaries</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="work-a-segmentation-case"> <a href="#work-a-segmentation-case" title="Work a Segmentation Case">Work a Segmentation Case</a> <a href="#work-a-segmentation-case" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Work a Segmentation Case">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Illustrative scenario:</strong> a management-source scan reaches a training service, while an approved guest-source scan reports the same port as filtered. Both runs use the same method and time window. The service owner confirms the listener remained healthy throughout.</p> <p><strong>Analyze the difference</strong> before requesting more probes. Identify the policy question, the additional evidence needed, and the strongest conclusion supported by the two results alone. Assume the intended policy permits management access and denies guest access.</p> <p><strong>Expected reasoning:</strong> the observations are consistent with the intended separation. They do not identify the exact filtering device or prove every guest path is blocked. Correlate the test timestamps with the relevant network-control records to locate the enforced boundary.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Proposed statement</th> <th>Assessment</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>“The service was unavailable”</strong></td> <td>Contradicted by the management observation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>“The guest test did not reach an open service”</strong></td> <td>Supported within the recorded method and window</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>“Every guest access path is blocked”</strong></td> <td>Broader than the tested evidence</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="watch-the-nmap-presentation"> <a href="#watch-the-nmap-presentation" title="Watch the Nmap Presentation">Watch the Nmap Presentation</a> <a href="#watch-the-nmap-presentation" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Watch the Nmap Presentation">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Fyodor’s ShmooCon presentation</strong> explains network reconnaissance with Nmap. The official Nmap site hosts the presentation context and slides. Focus on how a probe produces evidence and how the observer interprets it. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the presentation page"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://nmap.org/presentations/Shmoo06/"> <a href="https://nmap.org/presentations/Shmoo06/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the presentation page</a> </span> .</p> <p><em>This talk is from 2006. Use the current manual for platform support, defaults, and option behavior.</em></p> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Fyodor - Advanced Network Reconnaissance with Nmap - ShmooCon 2006"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/OdpgbzsK_5E/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OdpgbzsK_5E"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="OdpgbzsK_5E" videotitle="Fyodor - Advanced Network Reconnaissance with Nmap - ShmooCon 2006" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OdpgbzsK_5E" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Fyodor - Advanced Network Reconnaissance with Nmap - ShmooCon 2006"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Fyodor - Advanced Network Reconnaissance with Nmap - ShmooCon 2006", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/OdpgbzsK_5E\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OdpgbzsK_5E", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Watch on YouTube:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Fyodor - Advanced Network Reconnaissance with Nmap - ShmooCon 2006"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OdpgbzsK_5E"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OdpgbzsK_5E" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Fyodor - Advanced Network Reconnaissance with Nmap - ShmooCon 2006</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="create-a-scan-manifest"> <a href="#create-a-scan-manifest" title="Create a Scan Manifest">Create a Scan Manifest</a> <a href="#create-a-scan-manifest" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create a Scan Manifest">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Design a bounded scan</strong> for an approved training service using the template below. Define the information needed, the smallest relevant port set, and the source from which the result matters. Include a stop condition tied to service health or a scope mismatch.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Scan ID and purpose: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Approved target and resolved address: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Source host, address, and network context: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Transport, ports, and exact command: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Tool version and required privileges: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Start/end timestamps and clock reference: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Expected observations: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Health checks and stopping conditions: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Raw output paths: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Observed states and reasons: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Uncertainty and proposed next action: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Review the manifest</strong> against the original question. A useful plan makes omitted coverage visible and records why further probing is justified. Keep scan evidence available for deconfliction even if no alert or finding resulted.</p> <h2 id="check-your-understanding"> <a href="#check-your-understanding" title="Check Your Understanding">Check Your Understanding</a> <a href="#check-your-understanding" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Check Your Understanding">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li><strong>Methods:</strong> why is a connect scan not inherently invisible?</li> <li><strong>States:</strong> what does filtered leave unresolved?</li> <li><strong>Labels:</strong> why is a port’s service label insufficient to identify an application?</li> <li><strong>Coverage:</strong> what did the loopback exercise leave untested?</li> </ol> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Methods</strong></td> <td>Completed connections and patterns remain observable</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>States</strong></td> <td>Whether the service is open beyond the filtering boundary</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Labels</strong></td> <td>Port conventions differ from observed protocol behavior</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Coverage</strong></td> <td>Other ports, UDP, remote routes, authentication, and application vulnerabilities</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Initial-access planning</strong> uses validated context and a separate assessment objective. Continue to <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 10: Initial Access, Phishing and Delivery"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/initial-access-phishing-and-delivery/"> <a href="/red-team-course/initial-access-phishing-and-delivery/" rel="follow me" >Module 10: Initial Access, Phishing and Delivery</a> </span> to distinguish delivery, user interaction, and execution evidence. Return to the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Red Team Course hub"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Red Team Course hub</a> </span> for the full sequence.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: CompTIA A+ (220-1202): Operational Procedures
item.category: "CompTIA A+ Course" , "Operational Procedures" , "Documentation" , "Change Management" , "Backups" , "IT Support" , "CompTIA Certification" , "Help Desk" , "Professionalism" , "IT Fundamentals"
item.description: Master operational procedures for the CompTIA A+ 220-1202 Core 2 exam. Learn documentation, change management, backups, safety, environmental controls, communication, scripting, and AI basics.
item.content:encoded: <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Click Here to Return To the CompTIA A+ Course Page"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus-start/"> <a href="/a-plus-start/" rel="follow me" >Click Here to Return To the CompTIA A+ Course Page</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Operational Procedures</strong> is <strong>21%</strong> of the <strong>CompTIA A+ 220-1202 Core 2</strong> exam. This module covers documentation, change management, backups, safety, environment, professionalism, scripting, remote access, and AI basics. <em>This domain is about doing the job correctly and professionally, not just technically.</em></p> <p>A great technician follows process. You document your work, manage change safely, back up before you break things, stay safe, and treat customers well. This module covers the professional habits that keep IT running and keep you employed.</p> <h2 id="documentation-best-practices"> <a href="#documentation-best-practices" title="Documentation Best Practices">Documentation Best Practices</a> <a href="#documentation-best-practices" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Documentation Best Practices">#</a> </h2> <p>You record everything so others can follow your work.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Document</th> <th>Purpose</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Ticketing system</strong></td> <td>Tracks issues and resolutions</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Asset management / CMDB</strong></td> <td>Inventories hardware and software</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)</strong></td> <td>Step-by-step process guides</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Knowledge base</strong></td> <td>Reusable how-to articles</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Network topology diagrams</strong></td> <td>Maps the network layout</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="change-management"> <a href="#change-management" title="Change Management">Change Management</a> <a href="#change-management" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Change Management">#</a> </h2> <p>You control change so it does not cause outages.</p> <ol> <li><strong>Request</strong> the change with a documented form.</li> <li><strong>Assess risk</strong> and the scope of impact.</li> <li><strong>Test in a sandbox</strong> before production.</li> <li><strong>Get approval</strong> from the change board.</li> <li><strong>Plan a rollback</strong> in case the change fails.</li> <li><strong>Implement</strong> during a maintenance window.</li> <li><strong>Document</strong> the result.</li> </ol> <p><em>A rollback plan is what saves you when a change goes wrong.</em></p> <h2 id="backup-and-recovery"> <a href="#backup-and-recovery" title="Backup and Recovery">Backup and Recovery</a> <a href="#backup-and-recovery" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Backup and Recovery">#</a> </h2> <p>You protect data with the right backup type and rule.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Backup type</th> <th>What it copies</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Full</strong></td> <td>Everything, slowest</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Incremental</strong></td> <td>Changes since the last backup</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Differential</strong></td> <td>Changes since the last full</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Synthetic full</strong></td> <td>A full rebuilt from prior backups</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The <strong>3-2-1 rule</strong> keeps <strong>3</strong> copies of data on <strong>2</strong> media types with <strong>1</strong> copy offsite. <em>Test restores regularly because an untested backup is not a backup.</em></p> <h2 id="safety-procedures"> <a href="#safety-procedures" title="Safety Procedures">Safety Procedures</a> <a href="#safety-procedures" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Safety Procedures">#</a> </h2> <p>You protect yourself and the equipment.</p> <ul> <li><strong>ESD straps and mats</strong> prevent static damage to components.</li> <li><strong>Electrical safety</strong> means unplugging before service and never opening a PSU or CRT.</li> <li><strong>Proper lifting</strong> uses the legs, not the back.</li> <li><strong>Fire safety</strong> uses a Class C extinguisher for electrical fires.</li> </ul> <h2 id="environmental-controls"> <a href="#environmental-controls" title="Environmental Controls">Environmental Controls</a> <a href="#environmental-controls" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Environmental Controls">#</a> </h2> <p>You handle materials and power responsibly.</p> <ul> <li><strong>MSDS/SDS</strong> sheets describe safe handling and disposal of chemicals.</li> <li><strong>Battery and toner disposal</strong> follows local regulations, never the trash.</li> <li>A <strong>UPS</strong> provides battery backup and clean power during outages.</li> <li>A <strong>surge suppressor</strong> protects against voltage spikes.</li> <li>Maintain proper <strong>temperature and humidity</strong> to prevent damage and static.</li> </ul> <h2 id="policies-privacy-and-professionalism"> <a href="#policies-privacy-and-professionalism" title="Policies, Privacy, and Professionalism">Policies, Privacy, and Professionalism</a> <a href="#policies-privacy-and-professionalism" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Policies, Privacy, and Professionalism">#</a> </h2> <p>You follow legal and ethical rules.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Chain of custody</strong> documents evidence handling for incidents.</li> <li><strong>DRM and EULA</strong> govern software licensing and use.</li> <li><strong>Regulated data</strong> like PII, PHI, and PCI requires special handling.</li> <li><strong>Acceptable Use Policies (AUPs)</strong> define proper use of company systems.</li> </ul> <p>You use <strong>professional communication</strong>: clear language, active listening, setting expectations, and respecting the customer. <em>Never argue or talk down to a user, even when they are wrong.</em></p> <h2 id="scripting-and-remote-access"> <a href="#scripting-and-remote-access" title="Scripting and Remote Access">Scripting and Remote Access</a> <a href="#scripting-and-remote-access" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Scripting and Remote Access">#</a> </h2> <p>You automate tasks and support users remotely.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Extension</th> <th>Language</th> <th>Use</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>.bat</strong></td> <td>Batch</td> <td>Legacy Windows scripts</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>.ps1</strong></td> <td>PowerShell</td> <td>Windows automation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>.vbs</strong></td> <td>VBScript</td> <td>Older Windows automation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>.sh</strong></td> <td>Shell</td> <td>Linux/macOS automation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>.py</strong></td> <td>Python</td> <td>Cross-platform scripting</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>.js</strong></td> <td>JavaScript</td> <td>Web and automation</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Remote tool</th> <th>Use</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>RDP</strong></td> <td>Full Windows remote desktop</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>VPN</strong></td> <td>Secure tunnel to a network</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>SSH</strong></td> <td>Secure command-line access</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>VNC</strong></td> <td>Cross-platform screen sharing</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>RMM</strong></td> <td>Remote monitoring and management</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="ai-basics"> <a href="#ai-basics" title="AI Basics">AI Basics</a> <a href="#ai-basics" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="AI Basics">#</a> </h2> <p>The 220-1202 exam now includes basic AI concepts. You apply AI tools responsibly.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Application integration</strong> brings AI into business workflows.</li> <li><strong>AI policy</strong> covers appropriate use and plagiarism concerns.</li> <li><strong>AI limitations</strong> include <strong>bias</strong>, <strong>hallucinations</strong>, and accuracy problems, so verify AI output.</li> <li><strong>Private vs public AI</strong> differs in data security, data source, and privacy. <em>Never paste sensitive company data into a public AI tool.</em></li> </ul> <p>For the bigger picture, read <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="the state of AI in cybersecurity"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/state-of-ai-cybersecurity-2026/"> <a href="/articles/state-of-ai-cybersecurity-2026/" rel="follow me" >the state of AI in cybersecurity</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>You have now completed all nine A+ modules across both exams. Test your readiness with the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CompTIA A+ Practice Test"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus-practice-test/"> <a href="/a-plus-practice-test/" rel="follow me" >CompTIA A+ Practice Test</a> </span> , then review weak areas in <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Operating Systems"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus/operating-systems-windows-linux-macos/"> <a href="/a-plus/operating-systems-windows-linux-macos/" rel="follow me" >Operating Systems</a> </span> , <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Security"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus/security-threats-vulnerabilities-best-practices/"> <a href="/a-plus/security-threats-vulnerabilities-best-practices/" rel="follow me" >Security</a> </span> , and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Software Troubleshooting"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus/software-troubleshooting-windows-apps-malware/"> <a href="/a-plus/software-troubleshooting-windows-apps-malware/" rel="follow me" >Software Troubleshooting</a> </span> . Return to the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CompTIA A+ Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/a-plus-start/"> <a href="/a-plus-start/" rel="follow me" >CompTIA A+ Course</a> </span> and explore more in <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Courses and Playbooks"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/courses-and-playbooks/"> <a href="/courses-and-playbooks/" rel="follow me" >Courses and Playbooks</a> </span> .</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Module 10: Initial Access: Phishing and Delivery
item.description: Distinguish phishing delivery, interaction, execution, and access. Interpret campaign metrics, modern Office controls, and Windows architecture with worked examples.
item.content:encoded: <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="← Return to the Red Team Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course-start/"> <a href="/red-team-course-start/" rel="follow me" >← Return to the Red Team Course</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Initial access</strong> is the establishment of a usable starting context for an assessment. A delivered message, a clicked link, and code execution represent different outcomes. Your test should identify which boundary it examines and collect evidence appropriate to the tested boundary.</p> <p><em>Allow about 20 minutes, plus time to design the simulation record. The worked examples use synthetic events and require no messages sent to real recipients.</em></p> <h2 id="what-you-will-learn"> <a href="#what-you-will-learn" title="What You Will Learn">What You Will Learn</a> <a href="#what-you-will-learn" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What You Will Learn">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Distinguish</strong> delivery, interaction, execution, and communication outcomes.</li> <li><strong>Explain</strong> how email, document, identity, and endpoint controls affect an access path.</li> <li><strong>Analyze</strong> a synthetic campaign’s rates and ambiguous events.</li> <li><strong>Evaluate</strong> whether two simulations support a fair comparison.</li> <li><strong>Create</strong> a bounded initial-access test specification and handover record.</li> </ul> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Term</th> <th>Meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Delivery</strong></td> <td>A message or artifact reaches the specified destination</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Interaction</strong></td> <td>A recorded action such as following a link</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Execution</strong></td> <td>Instructions run in an identified process and security context</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Foothold</strong></td> <td>Usable access within the assessment’s permitted scope</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Mark of the Web</strong></td> <td>Windows zone information associated with some downloaded files</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Simulation artifact</strong></td> <td>Harmless material used to exercise an agreed control or behavior</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="choose-the-access-boundary"> <a href="#choose-the-access-boundary" title="Choose the Access Boundary">Choose the Access Boundary</a> <a href="#choose-the-access-boundary" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Choose the Access Boundary">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Phishing</strong> is one initial-access technique, not a universally reliable route. Its outcome depends on the scenario, delivery path, controls, and user context. An assessment might instead examine a public application boundary or begin from a deliberately supplied test account.</p> <p><strong>Remote code execution</strong> means an input causes instructions to run remotely. An upload feature alone does not establish this condition. File validation, storage location, server configuration, execution permissions, and how the uploaded content is handled determine the effect.</p> <p><strong>A web shell</strong> is server-side code exposing a command interface through a web application. Its presence is an execution and access concern, not the ordinary outcome of every uploaded document. Keep a suspected upload weakness separate from proof of server-side execution. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read MITRE ATT&CK’s web-shell description"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/"> <a href="https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read MITRE ATT&CK’s web-shell description</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Proposed test</th> <th>Boundary examined</th> <th>Minimal useful proof</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Mail simulation</strong></td> <td>Delivery and recipient response</td> <td>Correlated message and interaction records</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Document-control test</strong></td> <td>Opening and execution policy</td> <td>Policy result for an inert test artifact</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Application assessment</strong></td> <td>Input handling and authorization</td> <td>Bounded reproducible behavior</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Assumed-access exercise</strong></td> <td>Controls after a defined starting point</td> <td>Documented supplied identity and privileges</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="trace-the-delivery-chain"> <a href="#trace-the-delivery-chain" title="Trace the Delivery Chain">Trace the Delivery Chain</a> <a href="#trace-the-delivery-chain" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Trace the Delivery Chain">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A message’s lifecycle</strong> crosses several independent controls. Sending infrastructure, receiving mail systems, clients, browsers, endpoint policy, and network access each contribute a possible outcome. Name the stage where the observation occurred instead of reporting every failure as “phishing blocked.”</p> <p><strong>Human interaction</strong> also needs interpretation. A tracking request does not necessarily establish a deliberate click by the recipient. Microsoft documents false positives caused by security applications and automated message inspection, including interactions with forwarded simulation messages. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the simulation FAQ"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/attack-simulation-training-faq"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/attack-simulation-training-faq" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the simulation FAQ</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Execution and callback evidence</strong> are separate again. Even an authorized test program which starts successfully might fail to reach its reporting endpoint. Use the task-state distinctions from <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Module 5"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/red-team-course/command-and-control-operations/"> <a href="/red-team-course/command-and-control-operations/" rel="follow me" >Module 5</a> </span> when recording these outcomes.</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/delivery-interaction-execution-boundaries.webp", "caption": "Four connected boxes distinguish message delivery, interpreted interaction, endpoint execution, and confirmed usable assessment access", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-22 04:18:56.287841186 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b324.942933623", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-22 04:18:56.287841186 +0000 UTC m=+324.942933623"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://simeononsecurity.com/delivery-interaction-execution-boundaries.webp" alt="Four connected boxes distinguish message delivery, interpreted interaction, endpoint execution, and confirmed usable assessment access"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>Each transition needs evidence beyond success at the previous stage</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="set-up-the-measurement"> <a href="#set-up-the-measurement" title="Set Up the Measurement">Set Up the Measurement</a> <a href="#set-up-the-measurement" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Set Up the Measurement">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Gophish campaign configuration</strong> combines recipients, an email template, a landing page, a sending profile, and scheduling details. Its campaign records track events for analysis. Review the platform’s event definitions before assigning stronger meanings to the displayed labels. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the Gophish campaign documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.getgophish.com/user-guide/documentation/campaigns"> <a href="https://docs.getgophish.com/user-guide/documentation/campaigns" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the Gophish campaign documentation</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>A sending profile</strong> defines the approved sending service and related settings. It does not inherently require impersonating an unrelated organization. A landing page also need not collect credentials, so choose an inert completion page when a link-following measurement meets the objective.</p> <p><strong>Training and control assessment</strong> differ in purpose. An awareness exercise measures recognition, reporting, and learning under defined conditions. A technical assessment measures whether the delivery and execution controls work along an agreed path, so changes which permit training delivery alter the technical test.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Measurement</th> <th>Useful evidence</th> <th>Limitation</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Delivered</strong></td> <td>Receiving-system or platform delivery record</td> <td>Does not prove the recipient read it</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Opened</strong></td> <td>Platform-defined observation</td> <td>Image handling and client behavior affect it</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Clicked</strong></td> <td>Correlated interaction record</td> <td>Automated inspection needs review</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Reported</strong></td> <td>User-reporting workflow event</td> <td>Platform coverage and timing differ</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Executed</strong></td> <td>Endpoint-side process and result evidence</td> <td>Does not prove usable remote access</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="account-for-document-controls"> <a href="#account-for-document-controls" title="Account for Document Controls">Account for Document Controls</a> <a href="#account-for-document-controls" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Account for Document Controls">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Office macro behavior</strong> depends on application version, file origin, and policy. Microsoft’s current guidance documents default blocking of macros from internet-sourced files in affected Office applications. An older demonstration of an attachment launching code is insufficient evidence of behavior on a current managed device. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read Microsoft’s macro-blocking guidance"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-apps/security/internet-macros-blocked"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-apps/security/internet-macros-blocked" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read Microsoft’s macro-blocking guidance</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Record the environment</strong> before testing a document control. Include the application build, delivery method, relevant policy, and observed warning or block. A harmless file with no executable content tests delivery or opening, but not whether a malicious macro would have executed.</p> <p><strong>Do not change the tested control mid-run</strong> merely to obtain a desired outcome. If the approved exercise needs an exception for training delivery, record the exception and narrow the conclusion accordingly. An intentionally permitted path does not establish the baseline control would have allowed it.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Test condition</th> <th>Conclusion boundary</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Inert attachment opens</strong></td> <td>File delivery and opening worked</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Macro policy blocks a test document</strong></td> <td>The observed policy prevented the tested execution path</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Training delivery exception enabled</strong></td> <td>Result applies to the exception configuration</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Different Office build used</strong></td> <td>Comparison needs a version qualification</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="work-through-campaign-rates"> <a href="#work-through-campaign-rates" title="Work Through Campaign Rates">Work Through Campaign Rates</a> <a href="#work-through-campaign-rates" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Work Through Campaign Rates">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Illustrative scenario:</strong> a simulation targets 100 approved training accounts. Ten messages fail delivery. Among the 90 delivered messages, the platform records 18 unique accounts with click events, and review identifies six of those accounts as automation-only events. Fifteen accounts report the message through the training workflow.</p> <p><strong>Calculate the rates</strong> before interpreting them. Use delivered accounts as the denominator for this exercise and count each account once per metric. The reporting and clicking groups might overlap, so do not add them as mutually exclusive categories.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Metric</th> <th>Calculation</th> <th>Result</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Delivery rate</strong></td> <td>90 / 100</td> <td>90%</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Raw recorded-click rate</strong></td> <td>18 / 90</td> <td>20%</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Reviewed user-click rate</strong></td> <td>12 / 90</td> <td>About 13.3%</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Reporting rate</strong></td> <td>15 / 90</td> <td>About 16.7%</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Expected reasoning:</strong> the raw click count overstates the reviewed user count in this synthetic dataset. Keep both values and document the review criteria rather than silently editing history. None of these rates establishes a compromised endpoint or a captured credential.</p> <p><strong>A stronger report</strong> includes delivery failures, ambiguous events, reporting delay, and the exact denominator. Microsoft provides several simulation and training reports with defined metrics, so use the relevant report’s definitions when interpreting a real export. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the reporting documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/attack-simulation-training-insights"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/attack-simulation-training-insights" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the reporting documentation</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="compare-difficulty-fairly"> <a href="#compare-difficulty-fairly" title="Compare Difficulty Fairly">Compare Difficulty Fairly</a> <a href="#compare-difficulty-fairly" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Compare Difficulty Fairly">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Different messages create different tasks</strong> for recipients. An obviously unrelated request and a plausible work-context message are not equivalent challenges. A lower click rate on the easier message does not establish improved recognition across all phishing scenarios.</p> <p><strong>The NIST Phish Scale</strong> provides a method for rating human phishing-detection difficulty. It considers message cues and premise alignment with the audience. Use its documented method alongside outcome metrics when comparing exercises. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the NIST Phish Scale User Guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.nist.gov/publications/nist-phish-scale-user-guide"> <a href="https://www.nist.gov/publications/nist-phish-scale-user-guide" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the NIST Phish Scale User Guide</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Compare like conditions</strong> wherever possible. Record audience, message difficulty, reporting tools, delivery exceptions, timing, and any preceding training. If several conditions changed, describe the combined result and avoid attributing it to one cause.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Comparison difference</th> <th>Possible effect</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>New recipient group</strong></td> <td>Different role context and prior experience</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Different message premise</strong></td> <td>Different detection difficulty</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Delivery-policy exception</strong></td> <td>Different exposure to the technical controls</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Automated-click filtering</strong></td> <td>Different measurement rather than changed behavior</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="inspect-architecture-context"> <a href="#inspect-architecture-context" title="Inspect Architecture Context">Inspect Architecture Context</a> <a href="#inspect-architecture-context" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Inspect Architecture Context">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Windows process architecture</strong> matters when interpreting a subsequent test. Starting a service or using a particular operator command does not automatically imply a 32-bit process. Verify the actual process, operating system, and artifact architecture instead of inferring them from the workflow’s name.</p> <p><strong>WOW64 filesystem redirection</strong> affects many accesses from 32-bit processes to the Windows system directory on 64-bit Windows. The <strong><code>Sysnative</code></strong> alias lets a 32-bit application address the native system directory. It is not an ordinary physical directory or a universal path for 64-bit applications. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read Microsoft’s filesystem-redirector documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winprog64/file-system-redirector"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winprog64/file-system-redirector" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read Microsoft’s filesystem-redirector documentation</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>A read-only PowerShell check</strong> distinguishes the current shell process from the operating system. Run it inside the shell whose context you are examining. It says nothing about the architecture of an unrelated application.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>[<span style="color:#66d9ef">Environment</span>]::Is64BitOperatingSystem </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>[<span style="color:#66d9ef">Environment</span>]::Is64BitProcess </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Interpret the booleans</strong> in order. A true OS result and false process result indicate a 32-bit PowerShell process on a 64-bit operating system. Two true results indicate a 64-bit process on a 64-bit OS. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Read the .NET process-architecture property"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.is64bitprocess?view=net-9.0"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.environment.is64bitprocess?view=net-9.0" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Read the .NET process-architecture property</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="handle-unexpected-recipients"> <a href="#handle-unexpected-recipients" title="Handle Unexpected Recipients">Handle Unexpected Recipients</a> <a href="#handle-unexpected-recipients" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Handle Unexpected Recipients">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Forwarding and remote reading</strong> introduce scope uncertainty. A simulation URL tied to one recipient might be fetched from another device or by another person. Treat the correlation token as a record key, not proof of the operator’s identity or device ownership.</p> <p><strong>An unexpected interaction</strong> should trigger the agreed containment and review process. Stop any dependent assessment action, retain the minimal event evidence, and reconcile the event with the campaign owner. Avoid expanding endpoint access based only on a callback’s arrival.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Handover field</th> <th>Why it matters</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Message and recipient IDs</strong></td> <td>Correlate the planned delivery</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Observed interaction</strong></td> <td>Describe the event without assuming identity</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Endpoint identity</strong></td> <td>Confirm the approved asset where relevant</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Process and token context</strong></td> <td>Bound any execution claim</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Allowed next action</strong></td> <td>Prevent automatic expansion beyond the test</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="watch-the-simulation-overview"> <a href="#watch-the-simulation-overview" title="Watch the Simulation Overview">Watch the Simulation Overview</a> <a href="#watch-the-simulation-overview" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Watch the Simulation Overview">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Microsoft Security’s overview</strong> introduces Attack Simulation Training and its measurement purpose. Watch for how simulation outcomes lead to targeted learning and subsequent evaluation. Compare the presentation’s metrics with the denominator and ambiguity checks above.</p> <p><em>The video is an introductory 2021 presentation. Consult current product documentation for availability, UI details, and event semantics.</em></p> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Attack Simulation Training with Microsoft"> <meta itemprop="description" content="YouTube Video"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/zB_O-6bwZbc/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zB_O-6bwZbc"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="zB_O-6bwZbc" videotitle="Attack Simulation Training with Microsoft" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zB_O-6bwZbc" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Attack Simulation Training with Microsoft"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Attack Simulation Training with Microsoft", "description": "YouTube Video", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/zB_O-6bwZbc\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zB_O-6bwZbc", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Watch on YouTube:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Attack Simulation Training with Microsoft"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zB_O-6bwZbc"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zB_O-6bwZbc" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Attack Simulation Training with Microsoft</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="design-your-test-specification"> <a href="#design-your-test-specification" title="Design Your Test Specification">Design Your Test Specification</a> <a href="#design-your-test-specification" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Design Your Test Specification">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Create a specification</strong> for an inert link simulation using synthetic recipients. Define delivery evidence, a user-interaction criterion, an automated-event review rule, and a reporting objective. State explicitly which execution and access questions the simulation leaves unanswered.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Test ID and approved objective: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Recipients and excluded groups: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Sending service and artifact revision: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Landing-page behavior and collected fields: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Delivery window and stopping conditions: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Delivery evidence: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Interaction evidence and automation review: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Reporting metric and denominator: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Technical-control exceptions: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Unexpected-recipient handling: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Retention, owner, and follow-up: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Evaluate the design</strong> by applying it to the worked dataset. Another reader should reproduce the four rates and explain the remaining uncertainty. Revise any metric which labels a click as endpoint compromise without separate evidence.</p> <h2 id="check-your-understanding"> <a href="#check-your-understanding" title="Check Your Understanding">Check Your Understanding</a> <a href="#check-your-understanding" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Check Your Understanding">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li><strong>Stages:</strong> why is message delivery insufficient proof of execution?</li> <li><strong>Automation:</strong> what else generates a recorded link interaction?</li> <li><strong>Comparison:</strong> why does message difficulty matter when comparing rates?</li> <li><strong>Architecture:</strong> does a 64-bit OS prove the current process is 64-bit?</li> </ol> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Question</th> <th>Expected reasoning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Stages</strong></td> <td>Client, application, policy, and user-action boundaries remain</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Automation</strong></td> <td>Security inspection, link analysis, and other automated processing</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Comparison</strong></td> <td>The recipient’s recognition task changed</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Architecture</strong></td> <td>A 32-bit process also runs on supported 64-bit Windows systems</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Host awareness</strong> establishes what an approved starting context contains.
